notes: Eager backend advertises int8_linear on MPS but dispatches to CUDA-only torch._int_mm; community-validated dequant+F.linear fix, unmerged. All Apple Silicon int8 users hit it.
problem_text: On Apple Silicon, int8-quantized checkpoints (MiniMax H3, TRELLIS.2) die at the first linear of step 0: the eager backend lists int8_linear as a native op on MPS but fast_int8_mm calls torch._int_mm, which has no MPS kernel. Affects anyone running int8 models on MPS; nvfp4 (emulated) works fine, so it's a native/emulated classification gap.
solution_text: Community-validated fix in thread (Terralien-jp, confirmed by two other users): handle it in int8_linear by dequantizing the weight to activation dtype and running F.linear instead of falling back to fp32 inside fast_int8_mm (3.4x faster than the fp32 fallback, accuracy within int8 quantization error). Not merged upstream; unmeasured workaround: PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 (Maxim-Mazurok).
title: eager backend advertises int8_linear on MPS but dispatches to CUDA-only torch._int_mm

notes: OP-verified exact fix: dequantize 3 named BF16 tensors (learnable_registers, keyframes_abs_pos_embedding) post gguf_sd_loader; PR offered upstream.
problem_text: LTX-2.5 GGUF models have 3 BF16 non-layer params (learnable_registers, keyframes_abs_pos_embedding) left as GGMLTensor, so packed BF16 storage dims (e.g. 4096 vs 8192) leak into runtime ops and crash samplers.

title: LTX-2.5: BF16 non-layer parameters remain GGMLTensor and expose packed storage dimensions

notes: Maintainer-built wheel with API-probe graceful fallback, OP-confirmed with logs; affects all vGPU/virtualized-GPU users.
problem_text: On NVIDIA GRID/vGPU (RTX6000-24Q, A40-24Q), ModelVBAR(self.model_size()*10) raises a hard MemoryError('VBAR allocation failed') during model load because cuMemAddressReserve-based VBAR allocation fails in virtualized environments, instead of degrading gracefully to standard model management. Affects all vGPU/virtualized-GPU users; another user reports PyTorch >2.8.x correlation.
solution_text: Maintainer rattus128 built a new wheel (actions run 23231132334) with a startup self-test that probes the required CUDA APIs and wholesale disables the DynamicVRAM system when they fail; OP gregdotcom confirms 'Thanks for the new build, working fine now' with full success logs. Maintainer notes --novram mode is similar but switches aimdo off entirely, and suggests a no-vbar DynamicVRAM mode belongs in core ComfyUI.
title: bug & fix: ModelVBAR crashes on NVIDIA GRID / vGPU instead of falling back

notes: Hypervisor-level restriction (NVIDIA-confirmed) with maintainer-shipped graceful fallback, user-confirmed working; near-duplicate of #25 (Linux vs Windows vGPU).
problem_text: On Windows vGPU (and SR-IOV vGPU guests like L40S-48Q on Proxmox), cuMemAddressReserve returns error 801 'operation not supported' — NVIDIA confirmed Windows vGPU cannot open UVM and the hypervisor does not expose the VMM APIs — so VBAR/DynamicVRAM can never initialize there and cloud-provider Windows users are affected.
solution_text: Maintainer rattus128 shipped a wheel adding cuInit() plus an init-time probe of the required features so ComfyUI falls out of DynamicVRAM mode completely when they fail (comment with actions run 23231132334); Aanerud confirms 'The graceful fallback is working perfectly — ComfyUI no longer crashes, it just runs without Dynamic VRAM' and that the API is simply not exposed to vGPU guests (hypervisor-level restriction, not fixable client-side).
title: vGPU windows can't use comfy-aimdo

notes: Hardcoded 170-SM grid in launch.h; OP-verified one-line multiProcessorCount fix with profiler evidence; affects all non-5090 Blackwell SKUs.
problem_text: SA3 FP4 shows no speedup over SA2-FP8 on RTX PRO 5000 (110 SMs) vs the paper's 1.8x on RTX 5090; Nsight Compute shows the FP4 kernel launches grid=(170,1,1) because sageattn3/blackwell/launch.h hardcodes the 5090's 170 SM count, causing wave quantization on smaller Blackwell SKUs.
solution_text: OP-verified fix: replace the hardcoded 170 in launch.h with a runtime query (at::cuda::getCurrentDeviceProperties()->multiProcessorCount); after rebuild the grid becomes (110,1,1) and SM active utilization rises. Change not merged upstream.
title: SageAttention3 (Blackwell FP4): low speedup on RTX PRO 5000 (sm_120, 110 SMs)

notes: Best-documented: root cause read from 3.41 source — is_dedicated_install_allowed requires loopback bind regardless of allow_git_url_install flag; 13-comment multi-user confirmation. Workarounds only; no maintainer fix in-thread.
